function.name: client_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates of a single client based on the client's name and the status of the mandate. Partners can use this API to retrieve mandate information for their clients. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the client whose mandates are to be fetched.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If not specified, mandates with all statuses are retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches all mandates for all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the status of the mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of mandates to fetch. Possible values are 'active', 'pending', and 'inactive'.

function.name: partner_sips
function.description: Fetch all Systematic Investment Plans (SIPs) of all clients associated with a partner, filtered by the given status of the SIP. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the SIPs to be fetched. Valid statuses include 'active', 'stopped', and 'paused'.

message.content:
A **mandate** in financial services refers to an official authorization or instruction issued by a client (or investor) to a service provider—such as a bank, investment firm, or fintech platform—to act on their behalf regarding specific transactions or ongoing management tasks. Key aspects: | Feature | Description | |---------|-------------| | **Purpose** | Grants permission for actions like buying/selling securities, transferring funds, managing investments, etc., without requiring manual approval each time. | | **Types** | • *Active* – currently valid and enforceable.
• *Pending* – awaiting confirmation/activation.
• *Inactive* – expired, revoked, or otherwise no longer effective. | | **Scope** | Can cover one‑off trades, recurring orders, systematic investment plans (SIP), portfolio rebalancing, tax filing instructions, etc. | | **Legal Basis** | Often formalized through signed agreements, electronic consent forms, or regulatory filings depending on jurisdiction. | In practice, when you see “client mandates” or “partner mandates,” it usually means: 1. A list of all authorizations your organization has received from its clients. 2. Their current status (e.g., which ones are still active). 3. Any restrictions or conditions attached to them. If you need more detailed data—for example, retrieving all active mandates for a particular client—you would typically call an API endpoint such as `client_mandates(name="John Doe")` or query across partners using something akin to `partner_mandates(status="active")`.
